Senate.job: The winner is one of 100 votes on federal law, spending, treaties, and judges. The term is six years. The U.S. Senate has the sole power to conduct impeachment trials.

kurt alme.role: Former Montana budget director and revenue director.
kurt alme.bio: His campaign says he was born in Great Falls, graduated from high school in Miles City, and has worked as a prosecutor, nonprofit leader, revenue director, and budget director. He lives in Billings and is running for the Senate.
issues: He says that as revenue director he led the largest income-tax rate cut in state history and put money back with taxpayers.
He says that as budget director he helped cut spending and balance the budget.
He says he is running to make life more affordable, keep communities safe, and protect what he calls the Montana way of life.

alani bankhead.role: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and former federal agent.
alani bankhead.bio: Her campaign says she served 21 years in the Air Force and worked as a federal supervisory special agent on terror networks, spies, and child predators. She says she directed more than 180 agents across eight countries and is the Democratic nominee for Senate.
issues: She says she takes no corporate PAC money.
She says she backs I-194, which she calls The Montana Plan, to end dark money in Montana.
She says her public answers on issues are posted so voters can compare them with the other candidates.

seth bodnar.role: Former president of the University of Montana.
seth bodnar.bio: His campaign says he was raised by two public-school teachers, joined the military at 18, graduated from West Point, studied at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar, and served in Iraq as an infantry officer and as a Green Beret. He says he then led the University of Montana for eight years.
issues: He says he would try to end what he calls a costly and unauthorized war in Iran and stop tariffs he says are driving up prices.
He says he would work to lower health care, housing, and energy costs.
He says he would answer to Montanans rather than party leaders or corporate donors, and that he wants to end dark money and ban congressional insider trading.

kyle austin.bio: His campaign says he was born and raised on Montana's Hi-Line, worked his family's farm, earned a Doctor of Pharmacy, and founded an independent pharmacy. He is running for the Senate as a Libertarian.
issues: He says he still owns his grandfather's farm and wants policy that deals with the stress on farmers and ranchers.
He says he is a gun owner and hunter and wants Americans to keep unrestricted access to firearms.
He says his work as a pharmacist showed him corruption and other problems in health care.

troy downing.bio: The campaign says Troy Downing, a Republican combat veteran and businessman, represents Montana's 2nd District and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. Before Congress he was state auditor, securities and insurance commissioner, and a land-board commissioner.
issues: He says he advocates lower taxes, less regulation, and policies for economic growth, energy independence, and national security.
As insurance commissioner, the campaign says he held companies accountable and worked to keep rates down for families.
On the land board, he says he voted for more public-land access and for timber, oil and gas, and agriculture projects.
